Smart Property Data Trust Framework

Finance and Banking Working Group

You’re invited to help shape the Smart Property Data Trust Framework

Hello {{display_name}},

OPDA is bringing the property sector together to make UK property transaction data interoperable, verifiable and consent-driven. Today, the same information is repeatedly re-entered, translated and interpreted as it moves between organisations and systems. The OPDA Smart Property Data Standard will establish a shared language so that information can be understood, exchanged and reused with greater confidence.

Rather than forcing the whole property lifecycle into one universal model, OPDA is creating a governed family of connected domain models, each shaped by the people who understand that part of the market. Finance and Banking is one part of that wider standard. The models will preserve precise local meaning while allowing information to cross boundaries, and will support familiar outputs such as business glossaries, data dictionaries, schemas, APIs, forms and readable documentation.

You are not being asked to understand ontologies, adopt AI, or have technical knowledge. We ask you to share the material your organisation already uses, contribute your domain knowledge in Teams and challenge successive model drafts. OPDA will use an AI-assisted, human-governed process to turn that evidence and feedback into reviewable candidates, publishing and revising them with the group until the Finance and Banking model is ready to become its first official working-group draft.

I Accept
Sign in using the email account that received this invitation. This invitation link is unique to that account, so please do not forward this email.

🤝 Your contribution

There are three ways to take part:

  1. Share resources. Upload approved source material from your organisation as evidence for the model.
  2. Join the discussion. Contribute to relevant conversations in Teams and keep replies in their existing threads.
  3. Review model drafts. Provide feedback on model candidates published in Teams.

📤 How to contribute source material

  1. Open your company folder. Go to the Source Material Intake and select the folder named for your company. You will normally see only the organisation folder you are permitted to access.
  2. Organise your area as you need. You may upload files and create, edit, rename, move or delete folders, documents and notes in your organisation’s area.
  3. Keep a README at the top level. Include an index and enough explanation for OPDA to understand the contents. Keep it current as the material changes.

SharePoint uploads require an approved company-domain account. This does not affect participation in Teams. If your organisation needs another company account added for uploads, email smartdata@openpropdata.org.uk.

💬 How to participate

Reply in threads. With hundreds of participants, threads keep each subject together and make the discussion manageable.

Open the most relevant channel and check whether a thread already covers the subject. If it does, select Reply beneath the original post. The Start a post box creates a separate thread, so use it only for a genuinely new subject.

🧭 Where discussions happen

Announcements Official notices; read-only for participants.
Common Topics and Coordination Cross-cutting questions, coordination and whole-model review.
Mortgage Advice and Intermediation Advice, broking, suitability, sourcing, consent and application preparation.
Mortgage Lending and Underwriting Eligibility, affordability, underwriting, valuations, offers and lender decisions.
Mortgage Systems and Integration Platforms, sourcing, APIs, schemas, status exchange and integration.

Use the most specific channel that fits. Use Common Topics and Coordination when a subject crosses boundaries or concerns the working group as a whole.

🔐 Access and privacy

  • Invitation only. Access is limited to people invited by OPDA. To invite additional colleagues, email smartdata@openpropdata.org.uk with their names, email addresses and organisations.
  • Private organisation area. Approved company-domain contributors can view, create, upload, edit, rename, move and delete material in their organisation’s area. Other organisations cannot see it.
  • Permissions stay controlled. Contributors cannot view another organisation’s submissions, invite people, change permissions or make material public.

📚 Useful source material

  • Schemas and APIs: JSON Schemas; OpenAPI, Swagger and AsyncAPI definitions; GraphQL schemas; XML Schemas.
  • Database structures: database schemas, entity-relationship diagrams, data dictionaries and non-production DDL extracts.
  • Data and field lists: CSV, TSV, spreadsheets, JSON and XML.
  • Documents, guidance and blank forms: PDF, Word, Markdown and plain text.
  • Taxonomies, controlled vocabularies and semantic models: CSV, spreadsheets, Turtle/RDF, OWL and JSON-LD.
  • Diagrams and screenshots: draw.io, Visio, SVG, PNG, JPEG and PDF.
Audio and video files are not accepted. Recordings must be transcribed before submission. Include the transcript’s date, speakers and context where known.
Upload the material itself—do not submit links. OPDA will not follow links to websites, cloud drives, shared folders or online documents. If authorised, download or export the material and place the file in your company folder.

⛔ Do not submit

  • Personal, customer or live property-transaction data.
  • Passwords, API keys, credentials, private keys or other secrets.
  • Material restricted by confidentiality, contract, licence or NDA.
  • Executable software, active scripts or macros.
  • Password-protected files, encrypted archives or compressed archives.

What happens next

OPDA keeps the original source, reviews it for security and suitability, and uses approved information as evidence for AI-assisted data-model candidates. People review every candidate before it becomes a working-group draft. Source files are not automatically published or shared with other participants.

💬 Questions and model feedback: use the most relevant channel and reply in an existing thread whenever one covers the subject.

✉️ Additional invitations or private access problems: email smartdata@openpropdata.org.uk.
